params.name: Columns
params.note: Sent as a JSON attribute ([{ key, label, type, align, sortable, hidePhone }], camelCase). A column with a Cell template also fills the slot cell-<rowId>-<key> of each row.

params.name: Items
params.note: Sent as a JSON attribute (camelCase, one object per item, plus the row key "id" from IdOf).

params.name: IdOf
params.note: Wrapper parameter: writes the row key (the element is always given rowKey "id") and names each row's slots; without it the row index is the id.

params.name: DetailTemplate
params.note: The slot name is dynamic: the component renders one slot="detail-<rowId>" per row when Expandable is set, and only those rows get a toggle.

notes: Hand-written, generic: PkTable<TItem> (Components/PkTable.razor). Attributes down: the columns and the rows are JSON attributes (camelCase) rebuilt when the parameters are set, never per render and never through JavaScript. Events up: pk-sort, pk-filter, pk-select, pk-row-click and pk-row-expand reach the callbacks; the two-way parameters Sort, SortDirection, Filters, Selected and Expanded follow them (@bind-Sort and so on). Manual mode: the host owns the order, the filter and the page; the component shows Items as given and reports OnSort and OnFilter, and a PkPagination in FooterContent does the paging. Cell content: a column's Cell template is rendered as <span slot="cell-<rowId>-<key>"> per row, and DetailTemplate as <div slot="detail-<rowId>">; Blazor renders these as ordinary children of the element (the element reads them and never rewrites them), so a change of rows re-renders them together with the rows attribute. Without manual the element sorts, filters and pages its own rows.
